title: A perishable ability? The future of writing in the face of generative artificial intelligence
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether human writing ability could erode over time as generative artificial intelligence becomes more capable and widely used. Rather than presenting an empirical study, it makes a conceptual argument that writing may become a “nonperennial” technology: once a society can outsource routine writing to machines, the incentive for individuals to practice and maintain writing skills may decline.

The article develops this argument through historical analogy, especially the abandonment of Linear B in the Greek Dark Ages, and then connects it to current large language models such as ChatGPT. It includes examples of prompting ChatGPT to generate text, including a love letter and arguments about the possibility of skill loss, to illustrate how convincingly AI can produce human-like writing even without genuine emotion or understanding.

No population or educational intervention is studied. The paper’s main conclusion is cautionary: as AI text generation improves, humans may increasingly rely on machines for writing in many domains, which could reduce the practical need for human writing competence. The author also notes that current models still have important limitations, including reasoning failures, factual errors, and bias, but suggests that continued investment could make them substitutes for human writers in more contexts.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model chatbot and virtual assistant for generating and editing text via prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in an illustrative discussion and conversational examples about whether generative AI could erode human writing ability; the author prompted ChatGPT to generate a love letter and arguments about writing-skill loss.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/opinion preprint, not an empirical evaluation of ChatGPT or any educational intervention. It contains illustrative prompts and quoted outputs, but no systematic method, sample, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No impact estimate is reported and there is no measured educational effect. The paper discusses hypothetical risks and capabilities rather than demonstrating observable outcomes.
